children: Shares of Trio-Tech International rose after the semiconductor-solutions company received a three-year contract worth around $4.7 million at minimum with an new automotive semiconductor customer.
Shares were up 12% to $11.39 as of midday Thursday. The stock has risen 72% so far this year.

The company said Thursday that the three-year production burn-in contract supports a semiconductor application for electric vehicles. Trio-Tech did not identify the customer, but described it as a leading global integrated device manufacturer.
The contract requires minimum billings of about $4.7 million and has the potential to scale to $6 million, the company said.

"This three-year contract with our second EV semiconductor customer represents another important step in expanding Trio-Tech's automotive semiconductor business," Chief Executive S.W. Yong said. "The award provides meaningful multiyear revenue visibility while further validating our production burn-in capabilities with a new global IDM customer."
